validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: not in doubt. Transco (Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company, LLC) is the largest-volume interstate natural gas transmission system in the US, running from south Texas to New York City; it is documented by Williams' own corporate site (owner/operator), Wikipedia (independent secondary source with its own citations), Rextag (independent pipeline-data aggregator), an SEC-filed 10-K under Transco's own CIK, multiple FERC-docketed expansion projects (NESE, Gateway, Hillabee, Gulf Connector, Southeast Supply Enhancement) and decades of trade-press coverage (marked its 75th anniversary in Dec 2025). PipelineType='transmission' and Fuel='Gas' are unambiguously correct — this is the archetype of an interstate gas transmission trunk, not a gathering/process/feeder line. Status='operating' correct and current (actively expanding as of 2024-2025). DUPLICATE CHECK against the 45-row roster: P3296 ('Transcontinental Gas Pipeline | Station 65->Texas | len=0.0 cap=475.00') is NOT a duplicate/double-count of this row — it is a small distinct expansion-project segment on the Transco system (capacity 475 MMcf/d vs this row's system-wide 16,800 MMcf/d), consistent with how this tracker records a main-line system row alongside separately tracked expansion-project rows on the same physical pipeline. No fold recommended. HARVESTED CITATION POOL: 29 URLs harvested from gem.wiki. I opened/used 4 of them directly relevant to this row's SYSTEM-LEVEL specs (length/capacity/start year/location): eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php (already the sheet's own current_ref), rextag.com/pipeline/transcontinental-gas-pipeline (already the sheet's Capacity current_ref). The remaining ~25 (Kallanish, centraljersey, dec.ny.gov, nytimes, nj.com, grist, forbes, citylimits, stopthewilliamspipeline, investor.williams press releases on Hillabee/Gulf Connector/debt issuance, appvoices, hartenergy, EPA settlement, businesswire dividend, ijglobal x2, nola.com, virginiaplaces, sec.gov 10-K) describe SPECIFIC expansion projects, financings, legal fights, or an environmental settlement — none bear on the aggregate system-level length/capacity/start-year values this validity pass is checking, so they were screened by title/context and correctly not opened; they would matter for a segment-level row (e.g. NESE, Hillabee, Gulf Connector) but this row is the main-line system aggregate. I supplemented with fresh open-web search (Wikipedia, Williams.com, a 75th-anniversary trade-press piece) rather than relying only on the harvested pool, since the pool skews toward controversy/finance coverage rather than core specs.

validity.researcher_notes: LENGTH UNIT DEFECT (same family as the documented ASB Iraq/Libya mi-as-km escalations). GEM records LengthKnown=10200.00, LengthKnownUnits='km', and LengthKnownKm=10200.00 (i.e. the km-normalized column is a bare copy of the raw value, not an actual conversion — a strong tell no unit conversion ever happened). But every independent source on this pipeline states the ~10,000-10,500 figure in MILES, not km: (1) Rextag (rextag.com/pipeline/transcontinental-gas-pipeline, the sheet's OWN cited Capacity source) states 'Miles of Pipeline: 10000' and describes it as 'a 10,000-mile system from Texas to New York City'; (2) Wikipedia's Transcontinental Pipeline infobox states 'Length: 10,500 mi (16,900 km)' — i.e. Wikipedia's own editors give the km-equivalent, and it is ~16,900 km, not 10,500 km; (3) Williams' own corporate site (the operator) describes Transco as 'nearly 10,000 miles of pipelines.' Three independent origins (aggregator, encyclopedia, operator) all converge on ~10,000-10,500 MILES. If GEM's 10200 were actually kilometers it would be only ~6,340 miles, which contradicts every source and is physically too short for a Gulf-Coast-to-NYC mainline system with this many laterals. Tier high (3 independent sources). This is a value-affecting unit-label defect, not a request to silently retag — flagging as a concern per SOP rather than auto-correcting.

validity.researcher_notes: CAPACITY spec check (re-researched 2026-09-04, superseding the earlier rextag-only finding): GEM records Capacity=16800.00 MMcf/d cited to rextag, which itself now states 18.6 Bcf/d — neither is current. PINNED VALUE: "At December 31, 2025, Transco's system had a design capacity totaling approximately 20.6 MMdth/d" — Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company LLC / The Williams Companies joint Form 10-K for FY2025 (CIK 0000099250, accession 0000107263-26-000006, filed 2026-02-24, period 2025-12-31). MMdth/d = MMcf/d for pipeline-quality gas, so 20.6 MMdth/d = 20,600 MMcf/d. Basis is TOTAL SYSTEM design capacity, which matches this row's mainline/system scope. INTERNAL CHECK: the same filing itemizes the four 2025 in-service expansions — Commonwealth Energy Connector +0.1, Alabama Georgia Connector +0.1, Texas to Louisiana Energy Pathway +0.4, Southeast Energy Connector +0.2 MMdth/d — summing to exactly the 0.8 step from the FY2024 10-K's 19.8, so the figure is not a typo. WHY 16800 WAS ONCE RIGHT: the same-filer 10-K series runs 15.0 (2017), 16.7 (2018), 17.4 (2019), 17.9 (2020), 18.6 (2021), 18.6 (2022), 19.1 (2023), 19.8 (2024), 20.6 (2025) MMdth/d — 16,800 is the Dec-2018 value to ~1%, i.e. the sheet is one full expansion cycle behind and 23% low. CORROBORATION IS NOT INDEPENDENT: the FY2024 10-K (19.8 at 2024-12-31) is the same filer; Williams' April-2025 investor release ("system-design capacity has increased to over 20 Bcf/d") is the origin every trade-press repeat traces back to; williams.com's fact card (19.5 MMdth/d "peak design capacity") is undated and stale. EIA's State-to-State Capacity workbook (FERC Form 2 derived) is genuinely independent and shows Transco's tightest mainline link, PA->NJ, rising 4,812 -> 5,641 MMcf/d, corroborating the growth but on a point-to-point basis that cannot verify a system total. Hence tier medium, not high. GOES STALE AGAIN: the same 10-K schedules Gillis West (+115 Mdth/d, as early as Q2 2026), Southeast Supply Enhancement (+1,597 Mdth/d, FERC-approved Jan 2026, as early as Q3 2027) and Northeast Supply Enhancement (+400 Mdth/d, certificate reissued Aug 2025, as early as Q4 2027) — re-verify against the FY2026 10-K (expected ~Feb 2027).

fills.researcher_notes: Williams' own site: pipeline 'extends from south Texas to New York City' across 13 states. Rextag independently: 'a 10,000-mile system from Texas to New York City.' Both agree with GEM's recorded start (offshore Texas) / end (New York) endpoints; 'offshore' start is consistent with Transco's Gulf of Mexico production-area origin described in both sources.

Williams' own site states plainly: 'Williams owns and operates the nation's largest and most reliable interstate natural gas transmission pipeline, called Transco' (100% ownership implied — no co-owner ever mentioned anywhere in the sourcing). Wikipedia's infobox names the owner as 'Williams Companies' rather than 'Transco' specifically — a naming-level nuance (Transco/Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company, LLC is the wholly-owned operating subsidiary that legally holds the pipeline; Williams Companies is the ultimate parent), not a disagreement about who owns it. GEM's convention of recording the operating-subsidiary name ('Transco') as Owner1 is consistent with the sheet's own naming for this pipeline. Tier medium — one direct operator self-statement plus one independent tertiary source naming the parent, not two sources both independently naming the exact same legal entity.
